en.title: Capital One OA #18: Matrix Rotation with Fixed Diagonals
en.description: You are given a non-empty n×n square matrix and a non-negative count turns. In each turn, the elements on both main diagonals stay in place, and the remaining four triangular regions rotate 90 degrees clockwise: a non-diagonal element at original coordinate (r,c) moves to (c,n−1−r), with coordinates counted from 0. Output the matrix after repeating this turns times. This mapping matches the fixed original 5×5 example entry by entry; the public source image on the original page explicitly shows a clockwise rotation with both diagonals fixed.
en.input: The first line contains n turns, followed by n lines of n integers each, separated by whitespace; LF/CRLF line endings and a trailing EOF are accepted. The original gave no numeric upper bounds; this site publicly adapts them to Java types: n≥1 (a non-empty square matrix), elements in −2147483648..2147483647, and turns 0..2147483647. n is limited only by the existing 32MiB input budget, with no separate smaller cap; 4095 is derived from the shortest-encoding budget and is not a source constraint. Empty matrices and negative turn counts are not supported as extensions.
en.output: Output the rotated matrix as n lines of n integers each; do not output n.
en.explanation: The first public example keeps the original complete 5×5 input and output; both diagonals, 1/7/13/19/25 and 5/9/13/17/21, stay fixed. The second and third public examples are added by this site: a 2×2 matrix is entirely diagonal and stays unchanged after any number of turns; a 1×1 matrix and zero turns likewise leave the matrix unchanged. The source image was downloaded separately and bound to its own hash; this site does not claim that the fixed snapshot contains an accessible image.
hints: Four rotations restore the original matrix.
The non-diagonal elements form disjoint orbits of four.
The strict top triangle r<c<n−1−r contains exactly one representative of each orbit.
